official.deadline_note: No programme-wide deadline exists: Study in NL states the 2026-2027 application opened on 1 November 2025 and directs applicants to the institution's own closing date. Published for the 2027-2028 intake: Radboud University - OSIRIS application by 31 January 2027, 23:59 CET and complete by 14 February 2027, 23:59 CET; Utrecht University - before 1 February 2027, 23:59 CET.
official.application_cycle: 2027-2028 academic year per participating institution pages; the central page still lists the 2026-2027 cycle
official.status_note: The central Study in NL page publishes the 2026-2027 round (application opened 1 November 2025) and has not yet announced the 2027-2028 opening date; participating institutions have already published 2027-2028 deadlines of 31 January / 1 February 2027.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Study in NL: 'Please note that this is not a full-tuition scholarship.' Radboud University: 'Please note that this is not a full scholarship. The costs of living and studying in the Netherlands are not covered by the scholarship.'
official.funding_period: one-off, paid in the first year of studies
benefits: The scholarship amounts to EUR 5,000, received in the first year of your studies (Study in NL).
Utrecht University publishes three award tiers: EUR 5,000, EUR 10,000 and EUR 15,000, all paid in the first year of studies even for a two-year programme.

Radboud University: a maximum of 26 scholarships for the 2027-2028 academic year, always combined with the Radboud Scholarship Programme (RSP); applicants may be awarded both or just the RSP, never the NLS alone.
eligibility: You are applying for a full-time bachelor's or master's programme at one of the participating Dutch higher education institutions.
You meet the specific requirements of the institution of your choice (published on the institution's website).
You do not have a degree from an education institution in the Netherlands.

Radboud University: you are not eligible for the lower EU/EEA tuition fee for other reasons, have no degrees achieved in the Netherlands, and did not receive previous education in the Netherlands (exchange programmes excluded if part of a degree achieved outside the Netherlands).

Utrecht University: you must not be eligible for statutory tuition fees and must never have been enrolled at an educational institution in the Netherlands (an exchange stay does not make you ineligible).
requirements: Radboud University: submit the OSIRIS application by 31 January 2027, 23:59 CET at the latest; the application must be complete by 14 February 2027, 23:59 CET, and incomplete applications will not be considered for scholarship selection.
Radboud University: also apply for the Radboud Scholarship Programme - the NL Scholarship is always combined with the RSP and can never be awarded alone.
Radboud University: hand in proof of English proficiency before the 14 February 2027 deadline.
Utrecht University: apply before 1 February 2027, 23:59 CET; the application portal closes at that time and selection only starts after the deadline.
Utrecht University: complete the Statement of Financial Resources, showing a realistic plan covering the full nominal duration of the Master's programme.
Utrecht University: applications submitted between 27 January and 1 February cannot be updated or supplemented with missing information.
documents: Utrecht University: Statement of Financial Resources (PDF) demonstrating how the applicant will fund the full nominal duration of the programme.
Radboud University: an OSIRIS application free of incorrect, illegible or missing documents by the completeness deadline.
Radboud University: proof of English proficiency before 14 February 2027.
Any further documents named on the institution's own NL Scholarship webpage (these differ per institution).
selection_criteria: Radboud University - academic excellence: outstanding study results (grades, test scores, publications), relevancy of the previous degree, and the ranking of the university where previous degrees were obtained.

Radboud University - ambition: the quality and relevance of the motivation letter, promise shown by previous achievements, and life experience or extracurricular activities such as internships or volunteering.

Utrecht University: academic background as demonstrated in the master's programme application, motivation explaining the relevance of the time in the Netherlands and at Utrecht University to future goals, and the quality and feasibility of the financial plan.
Selection for the scholarship and admission to the programme are two separate processes; an admission offer does not imply selection.
coverage: A one-off grant of EUR 5,000 (higher tiers at some institutions), paid in the first year of studies.
Nothing more: Study in NL states it is not a full-tuition scholarship and Radboud University states the costs of living and studying in the Netherlands are not covered.
application_method: Choose a participating Dutch institution and an NL Scholarship-eligible programme (not every programme participates).
Apply for admission to that programme through the institution's own application system.
Radboud University: indicate during the OSIRIS application procedure for a Master's programme that you wish to apply for an NL Scholarship.

Utrecht University: log in to your OSIRIS Online Application account, locate 'NL Scholarship' under the dashboard, click 'View/Edit' for the scholarship linked to the chosen programme, open the application form, answer all required questions and submit.
Meet the institution's submission and completeness deadlines and upload all required documents.
Await the outcome published by the institution (around mid-April 2027 at Radboud; results aimed for mid-April at Utrecht).
official.application_route: Apply for admission to an eligible programme at a participating institution through its own system, then request the scholarship inside the same portal (OSIRIS at Radboud and Utrecht) before that institution's deadline
official.citizenship_residency: Non-EEA nationality required; no degree from a Dutch education institution; Radboud: not eligible for the lower EU/EEA tuition fee and no previous education in the Netherlands (exchange excluded); Utrecht: not eligible for statutory tuition fees and never enrolled at a Dutch institution
official.international_eligibility: Yes - the programme is specifically for international students from outside the EEA
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: The programme must be NL Scholarship-eligible at a participating institution; Radboud excludes Erasmus Mundus Master's programmes and joint-degree Master's programmes, and not every programme participates
official.description: The NL Scholarship (formerly known as Holland Scholarship) is meant for international students from outside the European Economic Area (EEA) who want to do their bachelor's or master's in the Netherlands. It is financed by the Dutch Ministry of Education, Culture and Science as well as several Dutch research universities and universities of applied sciences.
official.english_requirement: The central page publishes no test score; Radboud University requires applicants to meet the English language proficiency requirement of the Master's programme of their choice, and recommends submitting proof of English proficiency before the 14 February 2027 deadline

not_confirmed: central opening date for the 2027-2028 round (not yet published on the central page)
number of participating institutions and total awards for the 2027-2028 cycle (central page lists only the 2026-2027 participants)
a unified English test score (set per programme by each institution)
verification.notes: EUR 5,000 first-year amount, the 'not a full-tuition scholarship' wording, the four central eligibility criteria and participating-institution lists were taken from Study in NL; institution deadlines, tiers and selection criteria were confirmed on the Radboud University and Utrecht University scholarship pages.

applicant_utility.summary: Treat this as a discount, not funding: the scholarship is a one-off EUR 5,000 (up to EUR 15,000 at Utrecht) paid in year one, and Study in NL states plainly that it is not a full-tuition scholarship, so you still need to finance non-EEA tuition and living costs yourself. Applying costs no extra paperwork at most institutions - you tick the NL Scholarship box inside your existing OSIRIS admission application - but which programme and which university you pick decides both the money and the deadline, because awards, tiers and closing dates are set per institution. Radboud bundles the award with its own Radboud Scholarship Programme application, while Utrecht runs three tiers and grades the feasibility of your financial plan, so identical applications can be worth very different amounts.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Non-EEA bachelor or master applicants to a participating Dutch institution who can fund the bulk of tuition and living costs themselves and want a first-year EUR 5,000-plus contribution.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your chosen programme is on the institution's NL Scholarship-eligible list before applying - participation varies by programme.
Submit the admission application in the institution's system and tick the NL Scholarship option inside the same application (OSIRIS at Radboud and Utrecht).
Diarise the institution's completeness deadline, not just the submission deadline - Radboud disqualifies incomplete files after 14 February 2027.
Have English proficiency proof ready before the completeness deadline (Radboud asks for it by 14 February 2027).
At Utrecht, complete the Statement of Financial Resources with a realistic plan covering the full nominal duration of the programme, not just year one.
Verify you hold no Dutch degree and no prior Dutch enrolment, and that you are not eligible for statutory/EU/EEA tuition.
common_rejection_risks: Applying to a programme that does not participate in the NL Scholarship at your chosen institution.
An incomplete OSIRIS file after the institution's completeness deadline - Radboud explicitly will not consider these for scholarship selection.
Assuming a single central deadline exists and missing the earlier institutional date (31 January at Radboud, 1 February at Utrecht).
Assuming an admission offer implies a scholarship - selection is a separate process.
At Radboud, expecting the NL Scholarship alone: it is always paired with the Radboud Scholarship Programme application.
At Utrecht, filing between 27 January and 1 February, when incomplete files can no longer be corrected.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The bulk of the cost remains yours: non-EEA institutional tuition, living costs, health insurance, visa/residence-permit costs and travel. The scholarship contributes only a one-off EUR 5,000 (higher tiers at some institutions) in the first year.
document_audit: OSIRIS uploads must be legible and complete - Radboud sends back applications with incorrect or missing documents and only resubmitted files count.
Utrecht's Statement of Financial Resources must be realistic across the full nominal programme duration; one-year plans are rejected in practice.
English test acceptance and validity windows are set by the degree programme, not the scholarship, so check the programme page early.
Proof of no prior Dutch education/enrolment may be requested beyond the online form; keep certificates and transcripts ready.
alerts: The 2027-2028 cycle is expected to open on 1 November 2026 (the 2026-2027 round opened on 1 November 2025), with most institution deadlines on 31 January-1 February 2027 - re-check the central page in November.
At Radboud the NL Scholarship is never awarded alone; failing the pairing with the Radboud Scholarship Programme forfeits both.
Utrecht freezes applications from 27 January to 1 February, so late filers cannot fix incomplete files - submit weeks earlier.
The programme was renamed from Holland Scholarship to NL Scholarship in June 2023; older material under the old name may be out of date.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Admission application and scholarship request go through the same institutional portal (OSIRIS at Radboud and Utrecht); the institution screens, selects after its deadline and publishes decisions around mid-April.

official.deadline_note: This is the ESE-administered deadline. Applications received - or incomplete - after the deadline will not be considered; applications are reviewed after 1 February 2027 and all applicants are informed of the outcome by e-mail by 13 March 2027.
official.status_note: The page is published for the 2027-2028 round: the application opens on 1 December 2026 and closes 31 January 2027 at 23:59. The page flags that the 'Amount and payment' section will be updated in the third week of November 2026.
official.tuition_coverage_note: The tuition fee will be waived, both for students paying the statutory fee or the institutional fee. For EEA/EU students the tuition fee would have been EUR 2,695. For non-EEA/EU students the tuition fee would have been EUR 21,000: EUR 2,695 of the tuition fee is waived through the scholarship and the residual of EUR 18,305 is paid by the school.
official.funding_period: maximum total value for one academic year
benefits: Tuition fee waived, both for students paying the statutory fee or the institutional fee.
Living allowance equal to EUR 1,200 per month, so EUR 14,400 for one academic year.
Personal allowance equal to EUR 249, granted once.
Immigration fee (if applicable) equal to EUR 228 waived.
Only the living allowance and personal allowance are transferred to the student's account; tuition and immigration fee are waived, not paid out.
eligibility: Designed for full-time first-year master students with excellent results, both from EEA and non-EEA countries.

Must have never been enrolled before as a full degree Master student at an educational institution in the Netherlands (a Pre-master programme at ESE followed by an ESE Master in 2027-2028 is allowed).
Must be admitted to one of: Master Accounting, Auditing and Control; Master Econometrics and Management Science; or Master Economics and Business.
Must have achieved excellent study results in the previous Bachelor programme: an average final result of at least grade 7.50 on a grading scale of 1-10.
Must be able to demonstrate the reason why the scholarship enlarges the opportunity to study at Erasmus School of Economics, via a detailed financial statement.
Not applicable to current ESE Master students.
requirements: Must have registered in Studielink for one of the eligible Master programmes at ESE and submitted the application documents in the EUR Application Portal before 1 February 2027.

Must eventually be enrolled no later than 1 September of the academic year for which the scholarship is requested; an admission offer is not required at the moment of application, but only students with an admission offer will be considered.

Must have completed the immigration application; the general deadline is 10 July, but scholarship applicants are instructed to send it by May at the latest, including the tuition fee, living-costs deposit and IND handling fee.

The scholarship applies to only one academic year and can only be received once, and only for the same programme for which admission was received - switching programmes after being awarded is not possible.
Only 1 type of scholarship will be awarded to 1 applicant; applying for multiple scholarships is allowed, but combinations will not be awarded.
Number of applications each year exceeds the number of available scholarships, so no rights can be derived from meeting the minimum criteria.
documents: Motivation letter stating motivation to study at ESE, evidence of being an excellent student, and why the scholarship would expand the opportunity to study (max. two A4, Arial, font size 11).
Financial statement describing the financial situation and the reason and need to receive the scholarship (max. one A4, Arial, font size 11).
Budget plan using the 'Budget plan' template published by ESE, explaining how the studies will be financed if awarded.
Certified copy of the most recent academic transcript containing a wet stamp and signature of a school official; screenshots of online portals are not accepted.
Certified statement from the educational institution confirming the obtained GPA, using the ESE GPA template or a home-university statement containing the same information.
selection_criteria: Excellent study results: an average final result of at least grade 7.50 on a grading scale of 1-10 in the previous Bachelor programme.
Demonstrated financial need and feasibility, evidenced by the financial statement and budget plan.
Consideration requires an admission offer at the moment of review; meeting the minimum criteria grants no rights because applications exceed available scholarships.
coverage: Tuition fee waived (statutory or institutional fee); for non-EEA students EUR 2,695 is waived through the scholarship and the school pays the residual EUR 18,305.
Living allowance of EUR 1,200 per month, i.e. EUR 14,400 for one academic year.
Personal allowance of EUR 249 granted once and immigration fee of EUR 228 waived if applicable.
application_method: Gather the five required documents: motivation letter, financial statement, budget plan on the EUR template, certified transcript and certified GPA statement.
Submit the application online via Osiris student (eur.osiris-student.nl).
Applications are reviewed after 1 February 2027 and all applicants are officially informed via e-mail about the outcome by 13 March 2027.
official.application_route: Online via Osiris student with the five required documents, alongside the Master's admission application submitted in the EUR Application Portal
official.citizenship_residency: Open to both EEA and non-EEA students for this ESE-administered award; the page states the scholarship is designed for students from both EEA and non-EEA countries
official.international_eligibility: Yes - open to EEA and non-EEA students
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Admission to Master Accounting, Auditing and Control, Master Econometrics and Management Science or Master Economics and Business at Erasmus School of Economics; not applicable to current ESE Master students
official.description: The Erasmus Trustfonds Scholarship is designed for full-time first-year master students with excellent results, both from EEA and non-EEA countries, and amounts to a maximum of EUR 17,500 for prospective Master students for the year 2027-2028. Students from other schools may also apply, but the ESE-administered round admits applicants to three named ESE Master programmes.
official.program_type: University scholarship administered by Erasmus School of Economics, Erasmus University Rotterdam
official.english_requirement: The scholarship page itself publishes no test score. For the eligible programmes, ESE's admission requirements (MSc Economics and Business) require at least: Academic IELTS 6.5 (subscore 6.5); TOEFL iBT new scores 91 total / 4.5 subscore, old scores 91 total / 22 subscore; Cambridge C1 Advanced 176; C2 Proficiency 180 (subscore 176); LanguageCert Academic 70 (subscore 65); PTE Academic 70 (subscore 65). Tests must be taken within two years of application and online tests are not accepted for visa and residence permit purposes (check the other two programmes' pages for identical figures).

not_confirmed: final 2027-2028 figures for the amount breakdown (the page states the section will be updated in the third week of November 2026)
travel or installation coverage (not mentioned on the page)
the number of scholarships available each year
identical English scores for the other two eligible programmes (checked MSc Economics and Business only)
verification.notes: Maximum EUR 17,500, the award breakdown (tuition waiver, EUR 1,200 monthly living allowance, EUR 249 personal allowance, EUR 228 immigration fee), the 1 December 2026 - 31 January 2027 window and the document list were all read from the ESE scholarship page; English test minima come from the ESE admission requirements page for MSc Economics and Business.

applicant_utility.summary: This is the biggest single award an incoming ESE master student can win: up to EUR 17,500 combining a tuition waiver (with the school covering the residual of a non-EEA fee), EUR 14,400 of living allowance, a EUR 249 personal allowance and the EUR 228 immigration fee. The channel is narrow - only applicants admitted to three named ESE programmes (Economics and Business; Econometrics and Management Science; Accounting, Auditing and Control) can apply, and a bachelor average of at least 7.5 makes it a high-achiever award. It is also one-per-customer: you may apply for several EUR scholarships, but only one type will ever be awarded to you, so this and other EUR awards are mutually exclusive in practice.
applicant_utility.best_fit: High-achieving incoming master students (bachelor average 7.5 or above) admitted to an ESE economics, econometrics or accounting programme who cannot finance the roughly EUR 21,000 non-EEA tuition themselves.
application_readiness_checklist: Secure the bachelor transcript and GPA statement early - both must be certified with a wet stamp and signature, which can take weeks.
Draft the motivation letter and financial statement to the exact caps: two A4 pages and one A4 page respectively, Arial 11.
Download the ESE budget plan template and fill it in rather than building your own spreadsheet.
Register in Studielink and complete the EUR Application Portal documents well before 1 February 2027.
Apply for the scholarship itself in Osiris student between 1 December 2026 and 31 January 2027.
Line up immigration documents by May 2027 and ensure enrolment completes by 1 September 2027.
common_rejection_risks: A transcript submitted as a portal screenshot or without a wet stamp - explicitly not accepted.
Over-length motivation letter (hard cap of two A4 pages) or a financial statement exceeding one A4 page.
Applying without ever obtaining an admission offer - only students with an offer are considered at review time.
Bachelor average below 7.5 on the 1-10 scale, which is a stated minimum, not a guideline.
Switching to another master programme after the award - the scholarship is void if the programme changes.
Assuming this stacks with other EUR scholarships; only one type of scholarship is awarded per applicant.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: For a non-EEA student the tuition and immigration fee are waived, so the main uncovered items are housing and living costs above the EUR 1,200 monthly allowance, flights to the Netherlands, study materials, and anything for a second year (the award covers one academic year only). EEA students keep only the EUR 14,400 living allowance plus personal and immigration components.
document_audit: Wet stamp and signature on the transcript is non-negotiable; arrange notarised or certified copies through your university before December.
The GPA statement must contain the same information as ESE's template even when issued by your own university.
Motivation letter must do three jobs in two pages: motivation, evidence of excellence, and why the scholarship expands the opportunity to study at ESE - a generic CV letter will not score.
Immigration files (tuition fee, living-costs deposit, IND handling fee) should be ready by May, months before the general 10 July deadline.
alerts: The window is short: 1 December 2026 to 31 January 2027, 23:59, and late or incomplete applications are not considered at all.
The page flags that the amount and payment section will be updated in the third week of November 2026 - re-check the exact figures before budgeting.
You can receive the scholarship only once and only for one academic year, so a two-year master is half-covered at best.
Only one scholarship type is awarded per applicant, so prioritise: applying for both the Trustfonds and another EUR scholarship does not increase the chance of extra money.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Submit the five-document package in Osiris student between 1 December 2026 and 31 January 2027; the school reviews applications after 1 February and emails every applicant the outcome by 13 March 2027.
